_readme: Corrections to auto-computed badges for real-world facts the app's data
can't capture on its own (e.g. a season decided by extenuating
2012-2017 used to be hand-entered here too, since we believed ESPN had
no data at all for those seasons. That was wrong — ESPN's leagueHistory
endpoint serves them fine with valid espn_s2/SWID cookies (discovered
2026-08-15); build_badges() now computes them automatically from real
data like every other season, and every one of the removed hand-entered
entries matched the auto-computed result exactly before removal.
Valid types: champion, runner_up, reg_season_title, points_title, last_place.
team_id is the ESPN franchise slot id (see meta.json teams). If the franchise
no longer exists, use team_id: null and set team_name_then.
suppress[]: {season, type, team_id} — removes a specific auto-computed
badge before the badges[] additions above are applied, so a correction
reads as 'replace the wrong badge', not 'also show the wrong one'.
build.py applies suppress[] then merges badges[] into badges.json on every build.

badges.detail: Co-champion with Remember the Process, 2022 — the season's outcome was decided by extenuating real-world circumstances (the Damar Hamlin incident), and both finalists were formally credited as champions.
